This paper presents a method for object pose estimation that leverages the reliable scene geometry provided by depth projections to enhance the accuracy of the final result. Our approach begins by deriving a set of pose candidates through standard model-to-scene matching using depth image projections, followed by the aggregation of these candidates based on their 3D orientations. This study presents FedBuff, an innovative algorithm designed to accelerate and privateize the training of large language models within a federated environment. Furthermore, it introduces a buffer architecture to store these shards, enabling a buffer-to-buffer server-side Delta-Privacy scheme that ensures confidential aggregation of changes from various edges without transmitting full states. Results indicate that our method not only preserves the privacy and performance benefits of earlier algorithms but also substantially enhances communication efficiency by reducing the proportion of parameters exchanged during the learning process.

Extracting information-disasters from clinical notes can deepen the comprehension of patients' social determinants of health (SDH). Nevertheless, the unstructured and implicit nature of many SDH-related expressions within narratives presents a significant obstacle for automated extraction methods. This study proposes a new, targeted extraction framework designed specifically for SDHs in text. The proposed system operates in two stages: it initiates with an inline entity recognition phase, and subsequently employs an inline semantic interactions phase that builds upon those initial results to identify multi-word SDHs. The authors evaluated this framework on a narrative dataset derived from inpatient medical records, comprising 8,000 examples of SDH networked summaries manually annotated within texts. The results demonstrate that this two-step strategy outperformed single-phase text mining techniques, achieving 0.45 F-1 scores.

This study examines an optimally moving paddle swimmer within a periodic ratcheting flow, positioned at fixed points and switched between them at frequencies controlled by switch timing. By evaluating hydrodynamical interactions in both two and three dimensions, we observe that while average flow drives the swimmer, its interactions permit temporary displacement from expected locations. There is a compromise between switching frequency and the cost from hydrodynamic interactions and the time needed to reach the second average position. Ultimately, an optimal timing minimizes total cost by balancing these competing elements, even though it involves complex, non-trivial dynamics in multiple fluid environments.

The pandemic imposed global travel restrictions that stripped urban environments of their international encounters, disrupting urban lives and diminishing community resilience regarding future crises. This study analyzes the persistent impacts of these travel bans on urban diversity (2020-2022) by examining international travel statistics alongside UN data on urban encounter diversity. The findings indicate that even as travel resumed following the health crisis, the period significantly curtailed global diversity of encounters for the average individual over extended intervals. These observations carry critical implications for future strategies aimed at fostering cultural exposure and enhancing community resilience.

Annotated datasets are indispensable for training supervised models, yet annotator errors often introduce misleading labels that hinder model performance, creating a validation challenge since the ground truth for most tasks remains obscure. This work proposes a self-supervised technique to assess the reliability of annotated ground truth by utilizing a paraphrase task as the core metaphrase mechanism. The proposed framework is dataset-agnostic, requires no additional data collection or model retraining, and operates entirely in an unsupervised manner to label incorrect instances directly from the dataset itself. The methodology decodes each image caption into an image level of representation and decodes these visual representations back into paraphrased versions of the original texts using visual-linguistic projection heads; if two captions convey the identical meaning, their projections should exhibit high similarity. Empirical evidence from benchmarking three public datasets underscores the method's superior outcome when used to evaluate model accuracy. The study further validates that this approach, even when applied with dataset modifications, significantly enhances overall model performance by enabling more effective label filtering.

This paper introduces SPDP-DF, a new sampling method that uses the Dirichlet process (DP) as a prior for these structural parameters, offering a model approach. By estimating parameters directly, we can better capture the historical dynamics of population splitting and admixing events. Results from simulations and historical datasets show that this method effectively recovers admixture relationships and adds flexibility. The study highlights how different DP hyper-parameters affect the analysis. Furthermore, when SPDP-DF estimates parameters, it helps retrieve clear, identifiable mixing weight structures in the output, regardless of whether those weights are physically flipped during sampling; this holds true even if only a limited amount of genetic variation is available for estimation of the parameters. The SPDP-DF method offers a novel integration of genetic data analysis with population dynamics modeling, facilitating more comprehensive interpretations of evolutionary relationships between groups.

This research challenges the convention of modeling non-equilibrium clouds as simple layered systems with distinct clear and cloudy layers separated by radiative boundaries. We propose that many clouds contain an opaque "veiled core"—where internal radiative transfer is dominated by multiple scattering rather than radiative processes—that is covered by upper and/or side visible interfaces. To analyze this complex cloud geometry, we have developed a new mathematical framework for identifying cloud top and side boundaries in infrared and visible satellite images. The study then applies this model, incorporating advanced radiative transfer calculations, to re-analyze the classic single and double-layer equilibrium and non-equilibrium cases found in the literature. Notably, the observed "equilibrium" single layer in convective zones is reinterpreted through this lens as a system where an indistinguishable indeterminate core exists because its internal boundaries are masked.
